issues.issue: This paragraph says the Special Deposit "will be transferred by EMC to the Trust" on the Closing Date, while the definition of Special Deposit says it is "deposited into the Trust by the Depositor" and Section 2.01's granting clause conveys the Trust Fund from the Depositor. Who made the deposit, and therefore whose conveyance carries it, cannot be reconciled.

The Custodian must report documents that "appear to be defective on its face," a standard the Agreement nowhere defines and which the same sentence pairs with a right to "conclusively rely" on execution and genuineness. What counts as a reportable document defect, which drives the cure/repurchase remedy in Section 2.02(c), is left to construction.

The Final Certification exceptions must be notified only to "the Sellers," although Section 2.02(c) and (d) make the related Originator equally liable to cure, repurchase or substitute for document defects. The Originator receives no notice under this subsection even though its obligation is triggered by the same defect.

The last sentence makes cure, repurchase or substitution "the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf," without saying whether it bars money damages for a refusal to perform that obligation, and it omits the Trustee from the list of persons limited. The scope of the sole-remedy limitation is squarely open to argument.

The Trustee's duty to enforce the Sellers' repurchase obligations must be read against Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement, which makes cure, purchase or substitution "the Purchaser's, the Trustee's and the Certificateholder's sole and exclusive remedy" and fixes when a cause of action accrues. What the Trustee may enforce, and when, cannot be determined from this subsection alone.

The duty to give "prompt written notice" of a discovered breach is undefined as to time and says nothing about whether notice is a condition precedent to any repurchase obligation or an independent covenant whose breach is actionable. Both the meaning of "prompt" and the consequence of failing to give notice are left open.

The notice duty concerns breaches of representations "set forth in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or any Bring Down Agreement," and must be squared with Section 10 of that agreement, which independently requires notice on discovery and then gives MSMCH 90 days to cure, purchase or substitute. Whether this Agreement's notice paragraph adds anything to, or triggers, the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's protocol is contestable.

The bar on any substitution "following the second anniversary of the Closing Date" is stated to apply "[n]otwithstanding anything herein or in any other agreement to the contrary," but Section 2.05(a) suspends substitutions pending an Opinion of Counsel, which can push a required substitution past that deadline. The two provisions cannot both be given effect in that case.

The Purchase Price is due on "the Determination Date for the Distribution Date in the month following the month during which the related Seller or the related Originator became obligated to repurchase," but this Agreement never fixes when that obligation arises; Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement sets a 90-day period running from discovery or notice. When a repurchase is late has to be worked out across the two instruments.

The survival clause says "the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03 hereof" survive delivery of the Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files, but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's corporate representations, while the loan-level warranties that survive delivery are in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and the Bring Down Agreements. What survives, and for whose benefit, must be read across those documents.

The representation is made "as of the Closing Date, following the transfer of the Mortgage Loans to it by the Seller," but is then stated in the past tense ("the Depositor had good title"), leaving the moment at which title and freedom from offsets is warranted unclear. It also warrants only as to "the Seller" in the singular although there are two Sellers.

The notice duty is triggered "[u]pon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach," with no conjunction and no mention of the Master Servicer, Securities Administrator or Custodians who hold the files. Which parties owe the notice obligation is left uncertain.

The opinion precondition applies "[n]otwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement" and can defer a repurchase or substitution indefinitely, which cannot be squared with Section 2.03's flat two-year bar on substitutions or with the 90-day cure-or-repurchase period in Section 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. Which timing rule prevails is left unresolved.

Substitution for a non-qualified mortgage is permitted only "if the conditions in Section 2.03 and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or the Bring Down Agreements ... with respect to substitutions are satisfied," but Section 2.03 states no substitution conditions other than the two-year cutoff. The conditions to be satisfied must be assembled from the other agreements.

The final sentence forbids the Trust from engaging in any activity "other than in connection with the foregoing or other than as required or authorized by the terms of this Agreement while any Certificate is outstanding, and this Section 2.07," which is ungrammatical and leaves the restriction's content and duration uncertain. Whether the limitation lapses when no Certificate is outstanding cannot be read off the text.

This section requires the Master Servicer to "cause the Servicers to perform and observe" their covenants, an absolute obligation, while Section 4.03(b) limits the Master Servicer to enforcing those obligations and terminating a defaulting Servicer. Whether the Master Servicer guarantees Servicer performance or only polices it turns on reconciling the two sections.

The Trustee and Securities Administrator must "comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer" to preserve REMIC status, although the Seller is not a party to this Agreement and no standard limits such directions. The scope of that compliance duty, and how it interacts with the Trustee's own duties, is left open.

The closing sentence provides that nothing "shall impose any obligation on the part of the Trustee to assume or succeed to the duties or obligations of Wells Fargo or the Master Servicer unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer," so the exception swallows the disclaimer it qualifies. Whether the Trustee must step in is the opposite of what the sentence appears designed to say.

The fidelity bond and errors-and-omissions policy need only be "in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees," with no minimum amount, rating or benchmark. Whether coverage complies is unmeasurable on the face of the Agreement.

The obligation to return the Mortgage File is imposed by reference to "[s]uch trust receipt," although the preceding sentences describe only a request for release signed by a Servicing Officer and no trust receipt is provided for. The instrument creating the return obligation is unidentified.

The access sentence reads "The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access to information and documentation regarding the Mortgage Loans to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants at any time upon reasonable request," which omits conjunctions and leaves the class of persons entitled to access indeterminate. Who may demand the loan files under this subsection is a matter of construction.

Insurance collections are to be deposited "[p]ursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04" and made subject to withdrawal "pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04," although Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and has nothing to do with insurance proceeds. The deposit and withdrawal mechanics point to the wrong sections.

The Master Servicer must use its "best reasonable efforts" to cause Servicers to keep primary mortgage insurance in force, a hybrid standard the Agreement never defines and which differs from the "Accepted Master Servicing Practices" standard used elsewhere. What level of effort discharges the duty is open.

Amounts collected under Primary Mortgage Insurance Policies are to be handled "[p]ursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05," but Article V of this Agreement ends at Section 5.04. The cited authority for the deposit does not exist.

The proviso permits prior reimbursement of "any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances," a term the Agreement does not define, whereas the first sentence speaks of "Advances" and "other unreimbursed advances." What may be recovered out of REO rental income is therefore uncertain.

The Master Servicer and Securities Administrator must deliver the Annual Statement of Compliance "to the Depositor and the Securities Administrator," so the Securities Administrator is directed to deliver to itself, and the certificate covers performance under "this Agreement or other applicable Servicing Agreement" to which these parties are not signatories. What each signatory is certifying is unclear.

A failure to comply with Section 4.16 is "deemed an Event of Default" requiring immediate termination without cure, which cannot be squared with the Event of Default definition and notice-and-cure regime of Section 9.01, and the paragraph then declares that it "shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement." Which regime governs termination of the Master Servicer must be decided.

This paragraph likewise makes any Section 4.17 failure an Event of Default mandating immediate termination and declares itself to supersede "any other provision in this Agreement," colliding with Section 9.01's Event of Default and cure provisions and with the identically worded supersession clauses in Sections 4.16 and 4.18. Two or more clauses each claim to override the others.

The Depositor's comment window runs to "the 12th calendar day after the Distribution Date" only if the Securities Administrator forwarded the draft by the 10th, while the Master Servicer must sign by the 13th and the filing is due within 15 days, so the deadlines can overlap or fail entirely if the draft is late. Whose duty is breached when the chain slips is left to the general contingency proviso.

The Master Servicer must sign the Form 8-K by the close of business on the 3rd Business Day after the Reportable Event, while the Depositor's approval or changes are due only "no later than the close of business on the 3rd Business Day," so signature may be required before the review period ends. The sequence of review and execution cannot be performed as written.

Item (IV) requires "a Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D) below," but that certification is described in Section 4.18(a)(iii)(D); Section 4.18(a)(ii) concerns Form 8-K. The Form 10-K content requirement cites the wrong subsection.

The opening sentence is incomplete — "any Additional Form 10-D Disclosure, Additional Form 10- Disclosure or any Form 8-K Disclosure Information (collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information..." — so the defined term "Additional Disclosure" is never actually defined even though the rest of the Agreement uses it. What information the obligation covers is unascertainable from the text.

Contribution is to be made "in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties," with no method for measuring either factor or for resolving a dispute about them. The clause supplies a standard without any means of applying it.

This paragraph deems any Section 4.18 failure an Event of Default requiring immediate termination and declares that it supersedes "any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary," while its own final sentence and Section 9.01's Event of Default regime say otherwise; it also refers to termination "pursuant to this Section 4.18(d)," which is the e-mail notice subsection. Which provision governs a reporting failure cannot be settled within the section.

Section 4.18 may be amended "[n]otwithstanding the provisions of Section 12.01" without Certificateholder consent, which cannot be squared with the amendment and consent requirements Section 12.01 imposes for the Agreement as a whole. Whether reporting obligations can be rewritten without holders is a question of which clause controls.

The parties agree their obligations "will be supplemented and modified as necessary" by evolving interpretations, market "convention or consensus," or "advice of counsel," and that "no amendment of this Agreement shall be required" to effect such changes. What a party is actually obliged to do at any given time is left indeterminate.

This section imposes the filing obligation on "the Seller," but EMC and the Sponsor are not parties to this Agreement under the preliminary paragraph, and no other provision makes them subject to its covenants. Whether anyone is bound to make the UCC filings requires reading this section against the parties clause and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement.

The last sentence says "[t]his right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party," although the option it describes is conferred on Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder and not on the Seller. Who may assign the optional purchase right is contradicted within the same paragraph.

The Swap Account is created and maintained by the Swap Administrator, yet this subsection provides that investments are made on the Majority Class CE Certificateholder's direction and that "[i]n the absence of written instructions to the Securities Administrator" amounts remain uninvested, and it also refers to funds "of the Trustee held pursuant to this Agreement." Who holds and invests the Swap Account is inconsistent within the paragraph.

This subsection has the Securities Administrator establish the Reserve Fund on or before the Closing Date, while the definition of Reserve Fund says it is created and maintained "pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof." Which provision governs the fund's creation, and thus its permitted withdrawals, must be reconciled.
